g.text: One measurement, every market: product.csv to GraphQL, Merchant and the WMS
Weight, length, volume and distance kept once in SI with UN/ECE codes, converted exactly, and shown in each market's units only at the edge.
g, kg, oz or lb; 4 decimals
Lost, or typed into the body
MTR; as entered: cm or in
L × W × H per pack level
Store SI once, at full precision, with the unit as entered beside it: a 1 lb item is 0.45359237 kg and still knows it was 1 lb
Name units with UN/ECE Recommendation 20 codes (KGM, MTR, LTR, MTQ, KMT), the codes SAP's T006 ISO column and GS1 data use
Convert with exact factors: 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg, 1 in = 2.54 cm, 1 US gal = 3.785411784 L, 1 mi = 1.609344 km
Round only at the projection, to what each destination accepts: Merchant takes 4 decimals and in or cm; Shopify takes its own enums
Let the market choose the display: feedLabel and contentLanguage, ISO 3166 country, ISO 639 language, ISO 4217 currency
GTINs and parents aren't CSV-shaped: gtins is an array, variants nest (productSet) or share an itemGroupId (Merchant), and packs link child to parent
BigQuery and Vertex AI load after the channels: consented rows only, deduplicated by the idempotency key; the TypeScript event loader runs last
Not English by default: choose the language model by locale; for APAC, bge-m3 multilingual embeddings and m2m100 direct translation
Keep pack levels apart: each, case and pallet each carry weight, dimensions, volume and their own GTIN, so the WMS and the feed agree
Field names and unit lists are examples; check your SAP release, Shopify's metafield types and the Merchant product data specification. CRM Sync · Middleware vs AI Architecture
